newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain 96 Social security deficit overshoot - press.
newsitem.headline: Spain 96 Social security deficit overshoot - press.

text.p: Spanish social security ended 1996 with a deficit of 372.6 billion pesetas, overshooting the government's initial target by 150 billion pesetas, local press reported on Thursday.
It is also two percentage points over the initial government's goal at 0.3 percent of gross domestic product, financial daily Gaceta de los Negocios reported.
The Economy Ministry was not available for immediate comment on these figures.
But Spain's Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said yesterday the country had met for the first time its public deficit target (which includes the social security gap) at 4.4 percent of GDP.
The paper adds that the shortfall was mainly due to lower-than-expected social contributions, which were 200 billion lower than forecast.
